LESSON: WRITING 4.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: WhatsApp, among others, to peers, 1. Why do you write letters?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the key features of a formal letter
2. create a formal invitation letter using the correct format

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 4.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 4.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the key features of a formal letter

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the key features of a formal letter. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the key features of a formal letter.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the key features of a formal letter. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a formal invitation letter using the correct format

What this means
In this part you learn to create a formal invitation letter using the correct format. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a formal invitation letter using the correct format.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a formal invitation letter using the correct format. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the key features of a formal letter)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing to a partner. (skill: create a formal invitation letter using the correct format)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the key features of a formal letter.
3. Practise this skill: create a formal invitation letter using the correct format.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. WhatsApp, among others, to peers, 1. Why do you write letters?
2. Which kinds of letters do you write?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the key features of a formal letter.
5. Be able to: create a formal invitation letter using the correct format.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
